note: Australia's four largest banks are the Commonwealth Bank, Westpac, NAB and ANZ. ANZ's rates-and-fees page answers Incapsula's block (not passed) and Westpac's card comparison page answered 404 (2026-10-30), so the Commonwealth Bank and NAB are written. The Commonwealth Bank's personal credit card standard fees and charges (as at 29 September 2026, read 2026-10-30): Low Rate 6 dollars a month, a personalised purchase rate of 10.99% to 15.99% a year (this file's card since 2026-10-29, now written as that range), up to 55 days free; Low Fee 3 dollars a month, nothing in a month with 300 dollars spent, 20.99%, up to 55 days; Smart 19 dollars a month, nothing with 2,000 spent, 20.99%, up to 44 days; Ultimate 35 dollars a month, nothing with 4,000 spent, 20.99%, up to 44 days, no international fee (the Smart and Ultimate waivers end on 1 January 2027); cash advances 21.99% a year and a fee of 4.00 dollars or 3.00%, whichever is greater, at most 300; a late payment 20 dollars; the international transaction fee 3.50%. The Interest-free Low Fee card (10 dollars a month) and CommBank Neo (15, 20 or 25 dollars a month by a limit of 1,000, 2,000 or 3,000, written at 15) charge no interest and no international or late fee and allow no cash advances; their monthly fee is waived in a month with no transactions and the previous balance paid, which isn't written. The over-limit fee applies only to accounts opened before 1 July 2012 and isn't written. The page states no minimum payment. NAB's key facts sheet for its credit cards (correct as at 1 October 2026) and its personal credit card fees and charges (effective 1 October 2026), read 2026-10-30: the six cards on sale, each with its annual fee (Low Rate 99 dollars, Low Fee 49, Rewards 195, Rewards Travel 395, Qantas Rewards Premium 295, Qantas Rewards Signature 449), purchase rate (13.99% on the Low Rate, 22.49% on the others) and interest-free period (up to 55 days on the Low Rate, 44 on the others); cash advances 22.99% a year and a fee of 3.5%, at least 3.50 dollars; the minimum repayment 2% or 25 dollars, whichever is greater; a late payment 20 dollars (when the balance is 50 dollars or more); the international transaction fee 3.5% (none on the Rewards Travel card). NAB's older cards, no longer on the key facts sheet (Velocity, flybuys, Visa One, Low Rate Platinum and others), and the StraightUp card, whose rate isn't on the pages read, aren't written; nor are the 0% balance-transfer offers.
